demand.reason: Global cobalt consumption is estimated at roughly 200,000 metric tons annually, placing it securely within the high-demand band of 100,000–1,000,000 tons.

growth.reason: Demand is expanding moderately (6–12% CAGR), driven by the global expansion of electric vehicle batteries, aerospace superalloys, and rearmament trends, despite partial substitution toward cobalt-free LFP batteries in mass-market EVs.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) produced 230,000 of the 310,000 tons mined in 2025 (74%), placing primary mining diversity in the 65–85% band (Score 4).


Refining: Downstream chemical refinement into cobalt sulfate and high-purity metal is heavily concentrated in China, which controls approximately 80% of global processing capacity, mapping to the 65–85% band (Score 4).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: World reserves are about 12,000,000 tons. At 2025 mine output of 310,000 tons, they represent roughly 39 years of supply, tracking cleanly within the 30–50 year band.


Diversification: The DRC holds about half of world reserves (6.0 of 12 million tons) alongside Australia (14%). The resulting HHI of about 0.28 places the geographic endowment in the moderately concentrated band.

end_use.reason:
Defense & National Security (+1.5): essential in military jet engine superalloys and gas turbines. Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): forms the core of high-energy-density NMC lithium-ion batteries. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): utilized widely across EV battery platforms and automotive superalloys. Healthcare & Biomedical (+1.0): deployed in highly biocompatible cobalt-chromium orthopedic implants and radiotherapy isotopes.


Sector presence scores total 5.0 across 4 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus adds +1.5, yielding an objective composite score of 6.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) batteries act as commercially deployed zero-cobalt substitutes in EVs, though they carry energy-density trade-offs. Substitution in extreme-temperature superalloys remains highly limited (Score 2).


Recyclability: Global secondary recovery from new scrap, superalloy recycling, and expanding battery black mass operations supplies approximately 25% of consumption, placing it firmly in the moderate 20–40% recycling tier.

extraction_refining.reason: Cobalt extraction involves complex multi-stage processing. Copper-cobalt tailings require intensive hydrometallurgical refinement, while laterite ores demand massive capital for High-Pressure Acid Leaching (HPAL) autoclaves handling toxic intermediates, characterizing it as complex and specialized.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is adequate. Massive HPAL plant expansions across Indonesia are actively bringing significant new capacity online, reliably capable of adding 10–20% to global supply within 3–5 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India possesses zero commercial domestic extraction of primary cobalt. The nation is 100% import-dependent for superalloy manufacturing and EV battery precursors (Score 5).


Strategic Posture: KABIL has executed concrete plans in motion. Formalized frameworks with Australia and African diplomatic outreach include active due diligence on overseas cobalt assets with a 3–7 year timeline (Score 2).

price_volatility.reason: Cobalt prices experienced severe structural market swings, spiking over $90,000/ton before crashing below $30,000/ton. This movement far exceeds the 100% variance threshold, confirming high volatility driven by cyclical EV demand shocks.

capability.name: Cobalt
capability.next_move: Scale refining of imported hydroxide and black mass into battery-grade cobalt sulphate.
capability.what_india_has: Hydrometallurgical refining at Nicomet and Rubamin on imported intermediates and scrap; Rubamin also recovers cobalt from spent catalysts; CSIR-IMMT has a superalloy-scrap process; seabed nodule contracts.
capability.cost: No reliable public figure for a sulphate refinery. India's recycling scheme implies ~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr of recycling capacity (#15).

stages.india: None on land; seabed nodule contracts (366 Mt at 0.14% Co).
Nicomet and Rubamin refine imported feed and scrap (~2,060 t/yr).

stages.world: Cobalt sulphate into battery precursors: China 95%+.

strategyList.name: Permanent magnet making
strategyList.what: Alloying, strip casting, jet milling, pressing, sintering and coating (NdFeB); reduction-diffusion and sintering (SmCo).
strategyList.outside_china: China 94% of sintered magnets. Outside: Japan and Europe, with new plants such as Neo's in Estonia.
strategyList.cost: Neo (Estonia): over EUR 100 m for 2,000 t/yr, ~EUR 250 m to reach 5,000 t/yr. India's scheme: Rs 7,280 crore for 6,000 t/yr.
strategyList.india_base: IREL's 3 t/yr SmCo plant (Vizag); 20 bids for the magnet scheme (Aug 2026); DMRL and BARC know-how.
strategyList.gap: Scale; equipment; Dy/Tb-saving diffusion; qualification with motor makers.

strategyList.name: Laterite nickel: RKEF and HPAL (Indonesia's route)
strategyList.what: RKEF furnaces smelt laterite into nickel pig iron, ferronickel or matte; HPAL leaches it in autoclaves into mixed hydroxide (MHP) for batteries.
strategyList.outside_china: Indonesia (67% of mined nickel; leads refining growth); Philippines (HPAL feed refined in Japan).
strategyList.cost: Vale-Huayou Pomalaa (Indonesia): US$4.5 bn for mine and HPAL making 120 kt/yr Ni and 15 kt/yr Co in MHP.
strategyList.india_base: No laterite at scale; Sukinda overburden; CSIR-IMMT 10 t/day proving plant; ferroalloy furnaces.

strategyList.name: Nickel and cobalt refining to battery chemicals
strategyList.what: Leaching intermediates (MHP, matte, hydroxide), solvent extraction, crystallising nickel and cobalt sulphate.
strategyList.outside_china: China refines most cobalt; Indonesia is adding nickel refining; Finland and Japan are long-standing refiners.
strategyList.india_base: Nicomet (~6 kt/yr Ni), Rubamin (Co), Hindustan Copper (nickel sulphate), battery recyclers.
strategyList.gap: Feed contracts for MHP and hydroxide.

strategyList.name: Recycling (batteries, magnets, catalysts, PV)
strategyList.what: Shredding and hydrometallurgy of black mass; magnet recovery; spent-catalyst leaching; PV-panel recovery.
strategyList.outside_china: Battery recycling: China has over three-quarters of pre-treatment and 90% of material-recovery capacity; Europe, Japan, Korea and the US smaller.
strategyList.cost: India's scheme expects ~Rs 8,000 crore for 270+ kt/yr of capacity (~Rs 30 crore per kt/yr), yielding ~40 kt/yr of critical minerals.
strategyList.india_base: Lohum, Rubamin, the Bhopal magnet facility, CSIR-NML; Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme (2025).

chemistryList.name: Catalysts and spent-catalyst recovery
chemistryList.who: Rubamin (Mo, Co, Ni from spent catalyst); Hindustan Platinum (PGM refining).
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Molybdenum and cobalt recovery; catalyst-grade chemicals.
chemistryList.summary: Spent catalysts are concentrated secondary sources of useful metals. India already has industrial experience recovering molybdenum and other metals, alongside precious-metal refining. The opportunity is to connect traceable waste collection, selective recovery and customer-approved products, while distinguishing regeneration from destruction and metal recovery.

links.how: Some catalyst families contain these metals as active components or accumulated contaminants. Recovery depends on the actual feed and its assay. Rubamin identifies both among recoverable catalyst metals, but its battery-recycling compounds are described as industrial and technical grades; battery qualification must be established separately.
links.fit: Direct for suitable feeds; final grade remains product-specific

chemistryList.name: Hydrometallurgy and process R&D
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Tellurium from slime; nickel from overburden; magnet and battery recycling; REE separation flowsheets.
chemistryList.summary: Hydrometallurgy dissolves and separates elements into useful products. India has process-development experience, pilot facilities and some industrial transfers. That foundation can support several mineral chains; each feed still needs its own validated flowsheet and commercial case.

links.how: Can recover these metals from selected scrap, spent catalysts, batteries and refinery streams. NML lists transferred nickel-catalyst recovery and developed battery-recycling routes; IMMT’s overburden evidence is pilot-scale. The final metal or salt specification needs separate proof.
links.fit: Demonstrated transfer for selected feeds; other routes remain developmental
